penalties.authority: National Stock Exchange of India Limited
penalties.impact: The fine imposed on the Company has no material impact on the financial, operation or other activities of the Company. Due to delayed receipt of the Comptroller and Auditor General (C&AG) comments on the financial statements for FY 2025-26, the Company was unable to conduct the 27th Annual General Meeting within the timeline specified under Regulation 44 of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015. Upon receipt of C&AG comments on September 04, 2026, the Company had dispatched the Notice & Annual Report on September 07, 2026, and successfully conducted its 27th AGM on September 29, 2026. Since the Company has achieved the compliance of aforesaid Regulation, the application for waiver of fines as per SEBI's policy for exemption of fines, will be submitted in due course.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: As informed by counsel of IRCTC, case was heard on 15.07.2026. The Tribunal has given two weeks’ time to IRCTC to file the invoices along with the computation note, as a final opportunity.
tax_litigation.status: The GSTAT has passed final order on dated 14.10.2026 and has accepted the Directorate General of Anti-Profiteering (DGAP) Report and rejected all objections to the same. IRCTC has now been directed to deposit the profiteered amount as calculated, i.e Rs.50,41,44,461/- along with interest @ 18% as per Rule 133(3)(c) of the CGST Rules, 2017 w.e.f. 28.06.2019, in the Central Consumer Welfare Fund as well as in the State Consumer Welfare Funds in the ratio of 50:50 equally, in accordance with the state-wise bifurcation of the profiteering amount shown by the DGAP in its report within one month. It has further been directed that if the deposit of the profiteered amount plus interest is not made within 30 days, a further penalty of 10% will also apply. An appeal to the said order is being preferred before the Competent court of Jurisdiction. The same has also been informed to the exchanges vide our intimation dated 15.10.2026.

guidance.statement: Catering margin to return to the traditional 10-12% band as proof-of-concept trains wind down and the one-off HR cost does not recur.
Non-convenience fee to recover to about ₹150 Cr a quarter on iPay, e-wallet loyalty and agent-business changes.
Around 20 Vande Bharat sleeper trains may be introduced this year or next, with licence fee calibrated at ₹6 Cr to ₹120 Cr.
Tourism revenue may cross ₹1,000 Cr next year, from ₹890 Cr.

industry: Consumer Discretionary > Consumer Services > Leisure Services > Tour, Travel Related Services

operating_notes.text: Catering segment revenue rose to ₹670.88 Cr in Q4FY26 from ₹529.40 Cr a year earlier, but segment profit before tax fell to ₹41.90 Cr from ₹64.60 Cr.
Internet ticketing segment profit before tax was ₹297.77 Cr in Q4FY26, the largest contributor, against ₹306.93 Cr a year earlier.
FY26 exceptional income of ₹16.79 Cr included ₹580.49 lakh on reduction in fixed, variable and custody charges for two Tejas Express trains.
Internet ticketing commanded 89% market share of reserved railway tickets in FY26.
Rail Neer installed capacity is 17.77 lakh bottles a day against supply of about 15.5 lakh, with a ₹14 per bottle price point.
E-catering grew to about 1.69 lakh meals a day in FY27 from 1.05 lakh, and e-pantry covers more than 50 trains.
IRCTC's share of reserved railway tickets booked online rose to 88.92% from 88.78%, with 13.27 crore tickets booked in the quarter.
Signed MoU with Quality Council of India (QCI) for digital third-party food safety and hygiene audits across mobile and static catering units.
